Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 14:12:00 +0000
Subject: DPA: training data scope & EU transfer logistics

Oliver —

Thanks for the quick intro call earlier. Attached is our standard DPA with one proposed change highlighted for the training/model-improvement section. High level: Redwood’s standard position is that Customer Data will not be used to improve or retrain publicly available models unless the customer explicitly opts in. We do allow aggregate telemetry and performance metrics that are non-identifiable (see proposed language in section 3.2).

What we need from you to move to signature:
- Confirmation that your legal is comfortable with the proposed carve-out wording in section 3.2 (I’ve kept it narrow).
- Any procurement/vendor form or PO number we should reference on DocuSign.
- Confirmation on EU transfer mechanism: we can either include SCCs or execute under your preferred lawful basis — we usually attach SCCs for EU customers and have a standing export assessment available.

I’ve also attached our current subprocessor list and SOC 2 report for your security team. If it helps, I can loop in our privacy counsel (neha_kapoor) for any legal nuance.

If everything looks OK we can send the DPA via DocuSign and aim to have signed copies back in two business days.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Kimberly —

Thanks for the file. A couple of quick clarifications from our side before we push to legal:
1) The training carve-out language looks mostly OK but our counsel asks for a clear definition of "derive" and "de-identified" — we need to be sure there’s no backdoor that allows model updates with customer PII. Can you confirm that "de-identified" follows the EU GDPR anonymization standards (irreversibility)?
2) For transfers: we’d prefer SCCs be attached and referenced in the DPA; please confirm the exact SCC version you intend to use.
3) Procurement timeline: if legal signs off this Friday (23 July) we’ll onboard next week. If there’s any blocking redline from your side on training, let me know today so I can flag it.

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 09:30:00 +0000
Subject: RE: DPA: training data scope & EU transfer logistics (proposed legal redlines)

Kimberly / Marissa —

I reviewed the redline and recommend the following approach to keep the deal moving while protecting product IP and regulatory posture:

Proposed language (high level):
- "Training and Model Improvement": "Customer Data will not be used to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve Redwood’s models or shared weights that are available to third parties, except where Customer has provided explicit, documented opt-in. Redwood may collect and use aggregate, non-identifiable telemetry and usage metrics for system and performance improvements (for example, tokenization efficiency, latency metrics) provided those metrics cannot reasonably be re-identified to an individual or organization."

Key notes:
- Define "explicit opt-in" as a signed addendum or an in-product explicit checkbox with an auditable record.
- Define "non-identifiable" as consistent with GDPR guidance on anonymization (irreversible), not just pseudonymization.
- Attach SCCs v4 (if you use EU SCCs v4, call them out by name in the DPA and attach the full text).

For the subprocessor question, attach the current list and offer a 30-day notice for new subprocessors; for high-risk categories (HSM/KMS providers, model hosting partners), provide prior written notice and the option to terminate for cause.

I can prepare a short addendum that clarifies the opt-in flow and the precise anonymization definition; this tends to satisfy cautious legal teams.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Chang <oliver@kitebridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 15:45:00 +0000
Subject: Updated DPA + SCCs + subprocessor list (DocuSign ready)

Oliver —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. We incorporated Neha’s language into the DPA (see attached redline). Highlights:
- Training clause explicitly forbids use of Customer Data to train or improve models unless Customer provides explicit written opt-in (signed addendum or product opt-in).
- Allowed telemetry is limited to aggregate, non-identifiable metrics with an anonymization definition that references GDPR guidance.
- SCCs v4 have been attached and referenced in section 7.
- Subprocessor list attached; for HSM/KMS we will provide 14 days’ notice prior to onboarding and the contract allows termination for cause if the subprocessor materially changes processing scope.

DocuSign envelope: https://docusign.net/envelope/ABC12345 (I’ve pre-filled KiteBridge legal as signer).
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/KB-4391 (for reference).
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cExampleLink (full evidence pack).

If KiteBridge legal signs by end of day Friday (23 Jul) we’ll run provisioning for the pilot next Monday. Please let me know if they require any additional evidence (we can provide SOC2 logs, subprocessor contracts redacted, or KMS attestations).

Best,
Kimberly

Kimberly —

Thanks for the fast update and for looping Neha in. I’ve sent the DocuSign envelope to our legal team; they have one small ask around the anonymization definition (they want explicit language that anonymization is irreversible and cannot be reversed using reasonable ancillary information). I expect that to be a non-substantive tweak — can Neha add a short sentence to the definition inline and re-upload?

Also: procurement asked that the signed DPA reference PO #KB-2026-77 in DocuSign; I’ll forward the PO to you when our finance team confirms.

If you can make the anonymization sentence change today, we’ll accelerate signature and aim to return a countersigned copy by Friday.

Oliver
